summary: Harold Conklin worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at UC Berkeley (~1947–1950) and Yale (~1950–1955), and held a post at Columbia University (~1954–1962).
Harold G. Coward worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as a professor at the University of Calgary (~1974–1990) and held a post at the University of Victoria (~1990–2004).

Harold Hargreaves was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Officiating Director-General of Archæology in India at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1914 and from 1928 to 1931.

Harold Scheub studied at the University of Michigan (~1954–1960) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1969). He spent his academic career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2013).
Harold Stewart was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music and the University of Sydney.

Harold Walter Bailey worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. After studying at the University of Western Australia (~1921–1927), he served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge (1938–1967).
Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Chandrabhal Tripathi and held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.
Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme. He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel was an Indologist who served as Leiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1989) and worked in the Oriental Department of the Berlin State Library (attested 1992–1994).
Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his master's degree at the University of Tokyo. He held a professorship at Nagasaki University (attested 1988).
Haruka Yanagisawa worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1992–2005) and was affiliated with Chiba University (attested 2005).
Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA (1994) and PhD (2001) from UCLA, completing her doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson, an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar, earned degrees at Groningen and Leiden under multiple mentors. He held positions at Groningen, Oxford, the University of Pennsylvania (Professor, 2002–2006), and the University of Hamburg (Professor from 2006).
Harushige Kōzu was a linguist who studied at the University of Oxford (~1937–1939). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1942–1969) and Musashi University (~1969–1973).

Harvey B. Aronson, working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed his doctorate under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-director of the Dawn Mountain Center (attested 2001).
Haya Akegarasu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at the Tokyo School of Foreign Languages and Otani University (~1899–1902).
Heather Stoddard works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1966–1970) with D. C. Lau, under Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and under Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.
Hegoda Khemananda, a scholar in Buddhist studies, served as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya (both attested 1993).
Heidi Fjeld works in Tibetology. She earned her doctorate under Signe Howell at the University of Oslo (~2001–2006) and later held a postdoctoral fellowship there (~2007–2011).

Heidi I. Koppl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Sherab Zangpo.
